pattern_title: Mapping and classification gaps are inflating PPO Local spend
pattern_description: A large share of the increase sits in unclassified facility, DRG, and procedure buckets, especially in GA, CA, and CT PPO Local claims. The same issue shows up in clinical findings through blank or unknown procedures and recurring Not Mapped classifications in outpatient misc, nursing facility, and outpatient surgery categories. This is a gating issue because it can distort both authorization targeting and provider action if the underlying classification is wrong.

pattern_title: GA acute hospital spend is rising on both volume and unit cost
pattern_description: GA acute hospital spend in PPO Local is increasing from a combination of more claims and higher paid amounts per claim. Most of the increase is concentrated in claims that are not well classified, which makes it harder to separate true utilization growth from reimbursement or care-pattern change. There are also smaller mapped signals in circulatory and cerebrovascular cases, so this is not only a single-code issue.

pattern_title: GA non-acute site mix is adding cost across dialysis, SNF, rehab, and critical access
pattern_description: Beyond GA acute hospitals, spend is also moving up across several non-acute settings, led by dialysis and followed by SNF, physical rehab, and critical access facilities. The pattern is broad enough to justify a coordinated network and UM response rather than a single-provider intervention.

pattern_title: SNF costs are rising outside GA through a mix of rate pressure and emerging volume
pattern_description: Outside GA, PPO Local SNF spend is increasing across several states, with different mixes of price and volume pressure. CA and NY are more clearly unit-cost-led, while PA and the smaller CA / OH pattern show a mix of added claims and higher paid amounts. This is a post-acute reimbursement and care-routing issue that should be handled separately from acute hospital work.
